nodes.name: NiS2·WS2 Heterojunction Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Uniform flower-like NiS2·WS2 nanospheres were prepared by one-step hydrothermal reaction using sodium tungstate, nickel chloride, and thiourea as raw materials. The reaction temperature plays a key role in regulating the morphology of NiS2-WS2 heterostructure. Ultra-thin nanosheets with a thickness of about 10 nm are self-assembled to form flower-shaped nanospheres with an average diameter of about 2 μm by optimizing the experimental conditions.
nodes.source_text: Figure 1a shows the one-step hydrothermal synthesis of flower-like NiS2-WS2 heterojunction nanospheres materials using sodium tungstate, nickel chloride, and thiourea as raw materials... Uniform flower-like NiS2·WS2 nanospheres were prepared by optimizing the experimental conditions (Figure 1b).

nodes.name: Pure WS2 Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Pure WS2 was synthesized under the same conditions as NiS2·WS2 heterojunction (one-step hydrothermal reaction using sodium tungstate and thiourea as raw materials). Pure WS2 is a flower-like nanosphere with nanosheets aggregated.
nodes.source_text: For comparison, pure WS2 and NiS2 were synthesized under the same conditions (Figure S2, Supporting Information).

nodes.name: Pure NiS2 Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Pure NiS2 was synthesized under the same conditions as NiS2·WS2 heterojunction (one-step hydrothermal reaction using nickel chloride and thiourea as raw materials). Pure nickel sulfide is a small sphere of irregular particles.
nodes.source_text: For comparison, pure WS2 and NiS2 were synthesized under the same conditions (Figure S2, Supporting Information).

nodes.description: Full cell LSB performance with NiS₂·WS₂ + CNT-OH/PP functional intercalation (rate capability, cycling stability, high sulfur loading)
nodes.source_text: The initial discharge specific capacity of NiS₂·WS₂ + CNT-OH/PP is up to 1518.7mAhg⁻¹ at 0.2C. When the current density increases to 5C, the discharge capacity stabilizes at 697.3mAhg⁻¹... The specific capacity remains at 258.9mAhg⁻¹ after 1500 cycles with a decay of 0.039% per cycle... under the sulfur loading of 4.1mgcm⁻², ... remains at 3.2mAhcm⁻² after 100 cycles with a capacity retention rate of over 84.2%

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows uniform flower-like NiS₂·WS₂ nanospheres self-assembled from ultra-thin nanosheets with thickness ~10 nm and average diameter ~2 μm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Uniform flower-like NiS₂·WS₂ nanospheres were prepared by optimizing the experimental conditions (Figure 1b). Ultra-thin nanosheets with a thickness of about 10 nm (Figure 1c) are self-assembled to form flower-shaped nanospheres with an average diameter of about 2 μm (inset Figure 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms nanoflower spheres self-assembled from ultra-thin nanosheets; HRTEM shows lattice spacings of 0.283 nm (NiS₂ (200)) and 0.227 nm (WS₂ (103)).
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the transmission electron microscope (TEM) images in Figure 1d,e, the NiS₂·WS₂ nanoflower spheres are self-assembled from ultra-thin nanosheets... In addition, two different lattice fringes were observed in high-resolution TEM images (Figure 1f), where the lattice spacing of 0.283 and 0.227 nm corresponds to the NiS₂ (200) plane and WS₂ (103) plane.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDS mapping shows uniform distribution of Ni, W, and S elements, confirming uniform coupling of NiS₂ and WS₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, the EDS-Mapping (Figure 1h) shows uniform distribution of Ni, W, and S elements, which further proves the uniform coupling of NiS₂ and WS₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows crystal phases consistent with NiS₂ (PDF No. 11-0099) and WS₂ (PDF No. 08-0237); some NiS₂ peaks shift to lower angles indicating strong electronic interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a shows a series of crystal phases consistent with the characteristic diffraction peaks of NiS₂ (PDF No. 11-0099) and WS₂ (PDF No. 08-0237). Notably, compared with pure WS₂, the diffraction peaks of NiS₂·WS₂ coincide at 14.3°, 28.8°, 32.7°, 33.5°, 39.5°, 58.4°, and 60.5°. However, compared with pure NiS₂, some characteristic peaks of NiS₂·WS₂ shift to lower angles...

properties.peaks: Multiple diffraction peaks marked with symbols

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows WS₂ E₂g (350 cm⁻¹) and A₁g (416 cm⁻¹) modes with E₂g intensity equivalent to A₁g indicating NiS₂ heterojunction formation; E₂g shows slight blue shift.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiS₂·WS₂ shows two typical Raman peaks at 350 and 416 cm⁻¹, which correspond to E₂g and A₁g modes of WS₂. Interestingly, the intensity of E₂g of pure WS₂ is obviously lower than that of A₁g... In contrast, the strength of E₂g of NiS₂·WS₂ is roughly equivalent to that of A₁g, which indicates the formation of NiS₂ heterojunctions on the surface of WS₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey shows binding energies at 32.1 eV (W), 163.1 eV (S 2p), 284.6 eV (C), 538.7 eV (O), 886.2 eV (Ni); high-resolution spectra confirm phase composition with characteristic peak shifts indicating strong heterojunction interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2c, the binding energies at 32.1, 163.1, 284.6, 538.7, and 886.2 correspond to W, S, C, O, and Ni elements... As shown in Figure 2d, the peaks of binding energy at 163.1 and 164.2 eV correspond to S 2p₃/₂ and S 2p₁/₂ respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: UV-vis shows lowest characteristic absorption peaks intensity (250-300 nm) for NiS₂·WS₂ in Li₂S₆ solution, indicating strongest polysulfide adsorption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Uv-vis spectroscopy (Figure 3a) shows characteristic absorption peaks intensity of NiS₂·WS₂ from 250 to 300 nm is the lowest in the Li₂S₆ solution...
